root_cause.text: The DRM GEM shmem KUnit test called the internal `drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked()`/`drm_gem_shmem_vunmap_locked()` paths without first holding the object’s `dma_resv` reservation lock, violating the locking contract and triggering warnings in the shmem helper’s locked-page/pin/vmap code.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says to “Acquire and release the GEM object's reservation lock around vmap and vunmap operations,” notes that “The tests use vmap_locked, which led to errors,” and changes the test from `drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked(shmem, &map)` / `drm_gem_shmem_vunmap_locked(shmem, &map)` to new wrappers that call `dma_resv_lock_interruptible(obj->resv, NULL)` before `drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked()` and unlock afterward.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the KUnit visibility header so the file can use KUnit visibility support.
intent_record.what: A new include directive was added: `#include <kunit/visibility.h>`.
intent_record.how: This makes KUnit visibility helpers/macros available to the file at compile time, enabling code in this translation unit to use KUnit-specific visibility annotations or related declarations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add KUnit-only wrappers for drm_gem_shmem vmap and vunmap so tests can invoke the locked mapping helpers safely.
intent_record.what: Added a new KUnit-only helper section under CONFIG_KUNIT that defines and exports two functions: drm_gem_shmem_vmap(), which locks the GEM object's dma_resv, calls drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked(), unlocks, and returns the status; and drm_gem_shmem_vunmap(), which locks the same reservation object, calls drm_gem_shmem_vunmap_locked(), and unlocks. Both are exported with EXPORT_SYMBOL_IF_KUNIT.
intent_record.how: This makes the shmem GEM vmap/vunmap paths directly callable from KUnit tests while preserving the required reservation locking around the existing locked helpers. It enables test code to exercise the mapping logic without duplicating internal locking behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Import the KUnit testing namespace so the test module can use symbols exported for KUnit tests.
intent_record.what: A single line was added: `MODULE_IMPORT_NS("EXPORTED_FOR_KUNIT_TESTING");` near the top of the file, after the DRM helper includes and before the test size macros.
intent_record.how: This makes the module explicitly import the `EXPORTED_FOR_KUNIT_TESTING` symbol namespace, allowing the test code to link against symbols exported under that namespace at build/load time. It does not change runtime logic beyond enabling access to those exported test-only symbols.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the shmem vmap KUnit test to use the public vmap helper rather than the locked internal function.
intent_record.what: In the KUnit test `drm_gem_shmem_test_vmap`, the call to `drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked(shmem, &map)` was replaced with `drm_gem_shmem_vmap(shmem, &map)`.
intent_record.how: The test now exercises the public vmap entry point instead of the locked/internal variant, so it validates the normal runtime path used by callers and any locking performed by the wrapper itself.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch the vmap test to use the correct public vunmap helper instead of the locked internal variant.
intent_record.what: In the KUnit test `drm_gem_shmem_test_vmap()`, the call to `drm_gem_shmem_vunmap_locked(shmem, &map);` was changed to `drm_gem_shmem_vunmap(shmem, &map);`.
intent_record.how: The test now uses the public unmap helper instead of the locked variant, exercising the normal unmap path and its internal locking behavior rather than requiring the caller to hold the lock explicitly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Expose drm_gem_shmem vmap/vunmap helper prototypes to KUnit-enabled code for testing support.
intent_record.what: The header adds a new "Kunit helpers" comment block and, under `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_KUNIT)`, declares two functions: `drm_gem_shmem_vmap(struct drm_gem_shmem_object *shmem, struct iosys_map *map);` and `drm_gem_shmem_vunmap(struct drm_gem_shmem_object *shmem, struct iosys_map *map);`.
intent_record.how: When KUnit is enabled, other compilation units can now reference these vmap/vunmap helpers through the header, allowing test code to access or mock shmem mapping behavior without relying on implicit declarations.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a KUnit visibility header for test support. It does not address the locking contract violation around drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked()/vunmap_locked() or the missing dma_resv reservation lock that caused the warning.

The root cause is unsafe KUnit use of drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked()/vunmap_locked() without holding the dma_resv lock. This group adds KUnit-only wrappers and exposes the helper prototypes specifically so tests can invoke the locked mapping helpers safely, directly addressing that locking-contract issue.

The change only imports the KUnit testing namespace to access exported test symbols. It does not modify the DRM shmem test’s locking behavior or address the missing dma_resv reservation lock before calling drm_gem_shmem_vmap_locked()/vunmap_locked().

The root cause is that the KUnit test incorrectly called the locked internal shmem vmap/vunmap helpers without holding the reservation lock. This group explicitly changes the test to use the public vmap/vunmap helpers instead, directly addressing the locking violation.

candidates.rationale: This test directly calls the locked vmap helper without holding the object's dma_resv reservation lock, which violates the helper's locking contract and triggers the warning in the shmem locked-path code.
This test directly calls the locked vunmap helper without the required dma_resv reservation lock, exercising the invalid locked helper path and causing the warning described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call invokes the locked internal vmap helper without first acquiring the object's dma_resv reservation lock, which violates the helper's contract and triggers the locking warning in the shmem path.
This call invokes the locked internal vunmap helper without holding the required dma_resv reservation lock, exercising the invalid locked path and causing the warning described in the root cause.
